title: Supreme Court bails two Bilkis Bano convicts after 17 years in jail; Bano says she was not heard
dek: A two-judge bench suspended the life sentences of two men convicted of gang rape and murder in the 2002 Gujarat riots while their appeal is pending. Bilkis Bano says she learnt of the order from the press and will challenge it.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Supreme Court has suspended the life sentences of two men convicted of gang-raping Bilkis Bano and murdering members of her family during the 2002 Gujarat riots, and released them on bail while their appeal is heard, noting that they had been in jail for more than 17 years. Ms Bano said on Tuesday that she learnt of the order from press reports, that the court had not heard her, and that she would challenge it.

The order, passed on 28 October by a bench of Justices M.M. Sundresh and Prasanna B. Varale in the case of Bipinchand Kanaiyalal Joshi v. State of Gujarat, became public this week after it was uploaded. Reports name the second convict as Pradeep Mordhiya.

## What the court said

The two men argued that they had been imprisoned for more than 17 years; that one of them had not been named in the first information report and was implicated nearly three years later; and that one is severely handicapped, according to a summary of the order. The bench noted that the appellants "had been under incarceration for a period of more than 17 years", that one was "severely handicapped", and that the appeal raised issues "both on facts and law". It suspended their sentences and granted bail on terms to be set by the trial court, and directed that the appeal be listed for hearing in due course. No hearing date has been fixed.

The Gujarat government opposed bail. Additional Solicitor General Raja Thakre argued that the trial court and the High Court had both considered the evidence and the gravity of the crimes, according to the summary.

## Bilkis Bano's response

In a statement on Tuesday, Ms Bano asked how the court could "simply suspend the sentence of the men who did this to me", and said she was "scared once again" for herself, her family and her children, according to reports. "I learnt of this through press reports," she said. She said she would challenge the order, and that she was fighting for her three-year-old daughter and for women everywhere.

Ms Bano was 19 and pregnant when she was gang-raped by a mob during the 2002 Gujarat riots; seven members of her family were killed, according to reports. She has pursued the case for 24 years.

## Background

The Supreme Court moved the trial out of Gujarat to Maharashtra, where a special court in Mumbai convicted 11 men and sentenced them to life imprisonment. In May 2017 the Bombay High Court upheld the convictions and also convicted five police personnel and two doctors whom the trial court had acquitted.

In 2022 the Gujarat government granted remission to all 11 convicts under its July 1992 remission policy, after the Supreme Court had directed it to consider their application for early release. In a judgment on 8 January 2024 the Supreme Court set aside the remission orders and ordered all 11 to surrender within two weeks.

The new order does not overturn the convictions. The convictions stand while the appeal is pending.

## What happens next

The two men will be released once they meet the bail conditions set by the trial court. Ms Bano can ask the Supreme Court to recall or review the order. The appeals themselves will be heard later.
